title: Native STL surface reader and writer
overview: Native C++ STL surface reader and writer in OneFLOW Geometry. The implementation preserves source facets, binary headers and attributes while keeping parsing separate from topology construction. The Python grid/stl utility remains a separate planar-boundary and Gmsh-generation tool.
principle: STL stores an ordered sequence of triangle facets, not a shared-vertex mesh or CFD volume mesh. Preserve each facet's stored normal, ordered vertices, binary attribute value and binary header. Do not weld vertices, repair normals, infer units, invent boundary groups or assign solver boundary conditions during parsing. Binary records require explicit little-endian decoding; a header beginning with 'solid' is not proof of ASCII.
architecture: ASCII/Binary STL -> C++ StlMeshReader -> value-based StlMesh -> explicit validation -> explicit topology construction -> Mesh Core or downstream format adapters. StlMeshWriter serializes the same value model to ASCII or Binary STL. The adapter has no Gmsh, CGNS, Qt or Python dependency.
references: Library of Congress STL format description: https://www.loc.gov/preservation/digital/formats/fdd/fdd000504.shtml

proves: The C++ Geometry module provides native ASCII and Binary STL read/write APIs using a value-based facet model.
Binary parsing uses explicit little-endian field decoding and preserves the opaque header and 16-bit facet attribute.
ASCII and Binary STL writer/reader paths have linked native GoogleTest declarations for round-trip and malformed-data behavior.
does_not_prove: The STL surface has been welded into shared vertex topology or classified as manifold, closed or consistently oriented.
STL has been converted through the C++ adapter into OneFLOW Mesh Core, CGNS or a volume mesh.
STL carries units, named physical groups or solver boundary-condition semantics.
The linked GoogleTests have passed on every supported platform until CI execution evidence is recorded.
